# DESIGN.md — Dre's Island Food Services

archetype: editorial-agency
rationale: Dre's sells presentation as much as flavour ("we cater an experience"), and reviewers describe his displays as "perfectly curated canvases of color". An editorial-agency direction lets the plated work lead like a studio portfolio and sets the catering at the level its reviews and its $150 tasting event already claim.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [lavish, confident, sun-warmed, crafted]

typography:
  display: "Inter"
  body: "Source Sans 3"
  scale: 1.333
  notes: |
    - Inter is the brand face. Use it as a display face with a point of view, not as UI text.
    - Big statements: Inter 800 with tight negative tracking (-0.035em). The one headline per screen goes up to 7–8rem on desktop.
    - Section heads: 3rem at 700.
    - Eyebrows: Inter 600, 0.75rem, uppercase, tracked +0.14em.
    - Body: Source Sans 3 at 1.125rem, 1.6 line-height, measure no wider than 62ch.
    - Prices and dates: Inter with tabular figures.
    - One oversized type moment per screen. Everything around it stays quiet.

palette:
  primary: "#1f4a36"
  secondary: "#F3F4F6"
  accent: "#b08d57"
  ground: "#f5f2ea"
  surface: "#ebe5d6"
  ink: "#13261c"
  muted: "#4e5c53"
  border: "#d6cfbd"
  application: |
    Colour roles:
    - Primary green: carries whole panels at full bleed (the story block, the reviews band, the footer), so the brand is a surface rather than a button colour.
    - Secondary #F3F4F6: the text colour on those green panels (about 9:1 contrast).
    - Gold accent: the single action fill per screen, with ink text on it (about 5:1). It is also used for hairline rules and for large display figures on green, where it clears 3:1.
    - Gold is never used as small text on the light ground, where it falls below 3:1.
    - Ground: a warm parchment carrying a trace of the gold.
    - Ink: the brand green pushed nearly to black.
    - Muted: a green-grey that holds 5.5:1 on the surface.

    These neutrals come from the green and the gold of this brand, read as linen-and-brass event styling, and rule out a stock grey ramp.

composition:
  whitespace: generous
  photography: dominant
  card_usage: none
  mobile: |
    - Display type drops from about 7.5rem to 3rem. Line breaks are kept deliberate and are not left to reflow.
    - Asymmetric photo/type overlaps collapse to stacked image-then-text, with images cropped to 4:5 portrait so plated work fills the phone.
    - The gallery becomes a horizontal free-scroll strip.
    - The phone number becomes a tap-to-call link in the header.
    - Green panels keep full bleed.

pages:
  - slug: flavor-oasis
    title: Flavor Oasis Tasting Event | Dre's Island Food Services
    description: Flavor Oasis is Chef Dre's intimate tasting event in Wesley Chapel: curated tasting stations, live entertainment and island flavor, served beautifully.
    h1: Flavor Oasis
    intent: What is Chef Dre's tasting event, and what happens there?
    takes: [offerings]
    sources: [https://www.dresislandfoodservices.com/flavor-oasis, https://www.dresislandfoodservices.com/product/flavor-oasis/44]
  - slug: contact-us
    title: Book Catering | Dre's Island Food Services
    description: Planning an event? Tell Chef Dre about your date, guest count and the island flavors you have in mind, or call (772) 475-4460 to talk catering directly.
    h1: Tell us about your event
    intent: How do I get Chef Dre to cater my event?
    takes: [contact]
    sources: [https://www.dresislandfoodservices.com/contact-us]

  - from: /about
    to: index
  - from: /catering

  - from: /product/flavor-oasis/44

    to: none
  - from: /shop/difs-brunch-boxes/KTYKO6RVSRX35BOZQBSAUGTT

composition: |
  The work is the case. Nobody hires a caterer from a description, so the plated island food carries the argument at full scale. Selling copy is held back until the photographs have made it.

  Two voices give the page its authority:
  - Chef Dre's own line, "We don't just cater food, we cater an experience."
  - Clients who fed 80-plus guests and are still talking about it.

  Flavor Oasis is evidence of ambition, not the product. It gets a glance and its own page.

  There is no price list to lead with, and pretending otherwise would undercut the premium feel. The page closes the distance to a booking instead: every screen leaves the visitor one step from calling or enquiring.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Present Chef Dre's plated island dishes and grazing displays (the hero background images) as the most characteristic thing this business makes.
      - Set "Island flavor, served beautifully." as the oversized Inter statement.
      - Add one gold action that leads to booking catering on contact-us.html.
      - Put the phone number (772) 475-4460 within the frame.
  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Put a face and a philosophy behind the food.
      - Lead with their heading "We Don't Just Cater Food, We Cater an experience." at display size.
      - Name Chef Dre as founder.
      - Make clear that both drop-off and full-service orders get the same care over spice and presentation.
      - Write it in their own voice, not in agency copy.
  - id: gallery
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Show all eight gallery photographs as the portfolio, cropped and scaled editorially at varied sizes. This proves the "canvases of color" reviewers describe. There are no captions inventing dish names.
  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Make the reviews the strongest persuasion on the page.
      - Pull Camille York Adrien's "a symphony of sunshine and spice" as the page's one distinctive display moment, set huge on the green panel.
      - Set the other four reviews quietly beneath, each with the author's name.
      - Cover the range: an 80-guest housewarming, a last-minute rescue, a nonprofit Christmas party, a birthday weekend.
  - id: offerings
    priority: supporting
    show: "1 of 1, links to flavor-oasis.html"
    intent: |
      Present Flavor Oasis as the tasting event Chef Dre hosts, as evidence of the culinary ambition.
      - Labelled "Events", the business's own category, never "Menu".
      - Include the name, the description and the $150.00 price as recorded.
      - State honestly that the Second Edition (Sat, Aug 1) has ended.
      - Link through to the full page. No ticket or checkout button.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: "summary, links to contact-us.html"
    intent: |
      Close on how to book.
      - Show the phone number exactly as (772) 475-4460 and the address exactly as given (Factory 22, 6027 Wesley Grove Blvd, Wesley Chapel, FL 33544).
      - Add one clear route to the catering enquiry form on contact-us.html. That form posts with form_type "catering".

avoid:
  - The Dade City address from the business record. Use only the canonical Factory 22, Wesley Chapel address.
  - Any "Buy tickets", "Attend" or "Book your seat" action on Flavor Oasis, or any copy implying the Aug 1 edition is upcoming. The old site marks it as ended.
  - Invented dishes, platter names, package tiers or per-head prices. The only priced item is Flavor Oasis at $150.00.
  - Brunch boxes, an online shop or "Order online". No such content exists for this site.
  - Any nav item or link pointing to the old Square site's /s/shop, /s/order or /shop paths.
  - An email address, social icons, a newsletter, or opening hours. None of these are available.
  - Tropical clip-art clichés such as palm fronds, hibiscus, tiki or brush-script "island" fonts, steel-drum icons, or a sunset gradient.
  - The six Flavor Oasis highlight titles rendered as a three-column icon grid. On the Flavor Oasis page they are set as plain typographic lines.
  - Near-black with an electric accent. The dark surface here is the brand green, never #111.
  - Gold text at body size on the parchment ground.
  - A "Meet the team" section or page for a single person. Chef Dre lives in the story.
  - Star-rating graphics standing in for the actual review words.
  - Parallax for its own sake, and centring everything.
